lessons: WB went 3-0 tonight, contradicting the guide's 40% WB figure: two Victim of Night, two Chapel Geist, Slayer of the Wicked and Bonds of Faith did the work, so cheap removal plus fliers is the plan.
Take playable creatures late in pack 2: my picks 10-14 were Ancient Grudge twice, Brain Weevil (a guide skip) and Traitorous Blood, and none made the deck.
Committing to white-black by pick 5, with Victim of Night taken first and 12 Plains and 5 Swamp matching the pips, worked, supporting the guide's advice to settle a main colour early.
Commit to your two colours by mid-pack two: my pack 3 picks Brimstone Volley (pick 2) and Into the Maw of Hell (pick 4) were red and never reached my deck.
Cap top-end bloat: my black-green deck ran two Markov Patrician and went 3-5 in games, losing 20- and 22-turn games to WB, so favour cheap creatures.
Prioritise cheap black removal such as Dead Weight, Corpse Lunge and Tribute to Hunger; they were the core of the BG deck that won its round 3 match 2-1 against WU.
Tonight contradicted the guide's weak-WB rating: WB beat my WU 2-1 twice, and seat 0's WB went 3-0 with Victim of Night and Chapel Geist, so expect real WB removal.
Passing Prey Upon at pick 2 of pack 2 for Voiceless Spirit left my WU deck with no green flier answer in the 13-to-27-turn stalls I lost.
Opponents' WB decks held Rebuke, Fiend Hunter and Victim of Night for fliers, so keep at least four answers that can also clear ground blockers.
Consider 16 lands rather than 17 for a low-curve red-black aggro list: my 17-land build dropped Round 1 1-2 to WU, including a 27-turn game that aggro should not reach.
Take the second Dead Weight early: I picked two in Pack 3 (picks 1 and 3), and cheap black removal beside red creatures like Riot Devils and Stromkirk Patrol carried my Round 2 and 3 wins.

Tonight's WB deck went 2-1 with only one flier (Voiceless Spirit), contradicting the guide's four-finisher rule; Rebuke, Tribute to Hunger and Ghostly Possession carried it, but the 38-turn loss shows finishers still matter.
Pack 1's Runic Repetition and Wreath of Geists, and pack 2's Maw of the Mire and Graveyard Shovel, were dead picks. Take a playable flier or creature there instead, since pack 3 playables run thin.
Take a second evasive finisher over Walking Corpse. My 1-2 loss to UB ran 38, 17 and 22 turns, and my deck had one flier to break the stalls.
Removal alone did not carry this RG deck: Geistflame x2, Bramblecrush, and Spidery Grasp x2 went 3-5 in games, so prioritise a sturdy creature base alongside removal.

Round 3's BR opponent played Kruin Outlaw, Hanweir Watchkeep, Ashmouth Hound, and Crossway Vampire, all red or green cards in my colours, so commons you pass in your own colours can come back against you.
Galvanic Juggernaut and Pitchburn Devils were the top end, but I lost 0-2 to WB and 1-2 to BR, so draft early plays and cheap blockers before expensive finishers.
I took Brimstone Volley first and never played it, the unused-removal trap this guide warns about; take a P1p1 removal spell only if its colour stays open past pick 5.

The guide lists WU with fliers, cheap removal and a late threat as a working plan, but my four-flier WU went 0-3, losing games at 13 to 52 turns; take Stitched Drake or Spectral Rider over ground filler like a second Makeshift Mauler.
The guide lists Ghoulcaller's Bell as a skip, yet I took it last in pack 1, and both Traveler's Amulets I picked in pack 2 were cut; late picks should be playable creatures, since pack 3 runs thin.
Prioritise the blue fliers and cheap removal that carried this UB deck, Stitched Drake, Murder of Crows, Corpse Lunge and Sensory Deprivation, over filler like the two Fortress Crabs and Dream Twist.
Settle the second colour early: my 10 Island / 7 Swamp build had only a few black playables, which left the deck thin on answers, and I went 0-2 against WB.
Count the fliers your opponents can field: the WB deck that beat me 0-2 had Chapel Geist, Abbey Griffin and Manor Gargoyle, so keep Silent Departure-style answers in the main deck.
